segments.name: Retail
segments.description: Serves enterprise and mid-market retailers in convenience & fuel, grocery, drug & mass merchandise, and department & specialty retail with end-to-end commerce solutions.
segments.evidence: Our Retail segment primarily serves enterprise and mid-market retailers in the convenience & fuel; grocery, drug & mass merchandise; and department & specialty retail industries.

segments.name: Restaurants
segments.description: Serves quick-service, table-service and fast casual restaurants of all sizes with end-to-end solutions that streamline ordering and transacting.
segments.evidence: Our Restaurants segment is focused on serving restaurants and food service establishments including quick-service, table-service and fast casual restaurants of all sizes.

revenueModel.text: Retailers and restaurants pay for SaaS solutions, software licenses, hardware, payments processing, and installation, professional and maintenance services.
revenueModel.evidence: These decreases in revenue are partially offset by an increase in payment processing revenue, hardware revenue and hardware maintenance revenue as compared to the prior year.

changes.text: In 2023, the company spun off its ATM-focused businesses into NCR Atleos.
changes.evidence: On October 16, 2023, we completed the spin-off of our ATM-focused business, which included our self-service banking, payments & network, and telecommunications and technology businesses, into an independent publicly traded company, NCR Atleos Corporation and its consolidated subsidiaries (collectively hereinafter "NCR Atleos").

changes.text: In 2024, the company sold its Digital Banking segment businesses.
changes.evidence: We completed the sale of our Digital Banking segment businesses (the "Digital Banking Sale") to an affiliate of The Veritas Capital Fund VIII, L.P. (the "Buyer") on September 30, 2024.

changes.text: In 2024, the company entered an agreement to transition its self-checkout and point-of-sale hardware businesses to an outsourced design and manufacturing model.
changes.evidence: On August 6, 2024, we announced our entry into a commercial agreement with Ennoconn Corporation ("Ennoconn") to transition our self-checkout and point-of-sale hardware businesses to an outsourced design and manufacturing model ("ODM"), including the sale of certain assets relating to these businesses (the "Hardware Business Transition").
